obligations.title: Identification and traceability of outputs
obligations.interpretation: Where traceability is required, outputs are uniquely identified and the organization keeps the records that let each delivered output be traced back through production to the material and process history that justify its conformity.
obligations.intent: Each delivered lot can be traced back through production to the material and process records that justify its conformity.
obligations.expectedControl: A defined identification scheme carried through production; records linking delivered lot or serial to operations and to material and process certifications; retrieval without reconstruction by the auditee.

applicability.note: Applies where traceability is a requirement of the organization’s products or contracts; confirm against contracts and the scope of manufacture.

obligations.objective: Establish by tracing sampled shipped lots backwards that identification is maintained and traceability can actually be reconstructed.
obligations.method: Reverse trace from shipment: traveler → operations → material certification.
verificationActivities: Obtain the list of lots shipped in the last quarter
Select a sample across part families and shifts
For each lot, trace traveler → operation records → material cert
Confirm identifiers match at every hop
Confirm records are retrievable without reconstruction by the auditee
auditQuestions: Show how a lot identifier is assigned and where it first appears. What changes at each stage (kitting, machining, treatment, inspection, packing) and how is the link preserved when an identifier changes?
Choose a shipped lot and trace it backwards: shipment, traveler, each operation record, material certification. Which identifier ties each hop and who can retrieve it without help?
Where product is split, merged, reworked or scrapped, how is traceability kept for the remaining and the new quantities?
How is the material certification tied to the specific heat or lot used and not only to the part number? Show a case where two heats of one alloy were in stock.
How long are traceability records retained, where, and what happens when a record for a delivered lot cannot be found?
interviewQuestions: (Stores / production control) How is product labelled when it leaves kitting, and what do you do when a label is damaged or missing?
(Quality) The last time a customer asked for a trace, how long did it take and what was hard to find?
(Operator) If you split a batch at your station, what do you record and where?

sampling.guidance: Spread across part families; minimum 3 for a reverse-trace test of this size (auditor judgement; not an AQL plan).

riskConsiderations: Escape and recall scope depend on trace accuracy
Split or mixed-heat lots weaken the chain
A weak cert-to-lot link lets unapproved material pass unnoticed
commonFailureIndicators: Identifier changes between operations with no linking record
Material cert exists but cannot be tied to the lot
alternativeValidImplementations: Barcode or MES-based identification instead of a paper traveler
Serial-level traceability replacing lot-level where product is serialized
Supplier-held records, if retention and on-demand retrieval are demonstrated

aspects.text: Outputs carry unique identification through production
Traceability can be reconstructed from delivered lot back to material certification
Traceability records are retained and retrievable

obligations.shouldBe: Where traceability is required, outputs are uniquely identified and the organization retains the records needed to trace each output back to its material and process history.

obligations.title: Measuring equipment calibrated at defined intervals against traceable standards
obligations.interpretation: Equipment used to verify product conformity is calibrated or verified at specified intervals, or before use, against standards traceable to national or international references.
obligations.intent: Equipment used to accept product is demonstrably accurate at the time it is used, because it is calibrated within its interval against standards that trace to national or international references.
obligations.expectedControl: A calibration register with defined intervals; controlled status so out-of-interval equipment is not used; certificates showing traceable calibration; a response when equipment is found out of tolerance.

applicability.note: Applies wherever monitoring or measuring equipment is used to provide evidence of product conformity.

obligations.objective: Establish that equipment in use was within its calibration interval when used and that calibration is traceable.
obligations.method: Register review, then usage trace: pick equipment, compare its calibration status against records of when it was used.
verificationActivities: Obtain the calibration register for Plant 2
Select equipment, weighting toward product-acceptance tools
Compare due dates with the audit date
For any past-due item, trace usage records for the overdue period
Check certificates for traceability statements
Evaluate any extension, deviation or grace-period provision before concluding
auditQuestions: How are calibration intervals set for each equipment type, and on what evidence are they reviewed?
Compare the register due dates with today. For anything past due, what is its status and where is it physically?
For equipment that went past due during the review period, show the usage records for the overdue window. Was it used?
How is calibration status shown at the point of use and what actually stops use when it lapses?
Show a certificate: which reference standard is cited, what is the traceability statement, and were as-found results recorded and reviewed?
The last time equipment was found out of tolerance, what review of previously measured product was done and what was the outcome?
interviewQuestions: (Calibration coordinator) How are you reminded of due dates, and what happens when that system is unavailable?
(Operator) How do you know this tool is in date before you use it?
(Supervisor) If a tool is overdue and the job is urgent, what happens?

sampling.population: Calibrated equipment on Line 3 and Inspection
sampling.guidance: Prioritise product-acceptance equipment; include any past due on the register. Minimum 4.

riskConsiderations: Dependence on one person or one reminder system
commonFailureIndicators: Register is updated but usage is not checked against it
Past-due items stay "ACTIVE" in the register
alternativeValidImplementations: Verification against a master before each use instead of interval calibration, if defined and recorded
Interval adjustment based on documented history
Calibration in-house against traceable standards, or by a customer-approved laboratory

aspects.text: A calibration interval is defined for the equipment
Equipment was within its calibration interval when used
Calibration is against standards traceable to national or international references

rebuttalChecks.text: Authorized extension or deviation for the overdue item
Organization procedure provision for a grace period
Status identification at point of use

obligations.shouldBe: Measuring equipment used to verify product conformity is calibrated or verified at specified intervals, or before use, against measurement standards traceable to international or national standards.

obligations.title: Verification of externally provided processes and products
obligations.interpretation: The organization determines and performs the verification needed to be confident that what an external provider supplies meets requirements, and keeps evidence that it was performed.
obligations.intent: The organization decides, and then actually performs, the verification needed to be confident that what an external provider supplies meets requirements.
obligations.expectedControl: Defined verification per provider and product; performed on each receipt as defined; records retained where the organization controls them.

applicability.note: Applies where externally provided processes, products or services are used; scope the sample to the provider and output type in question.

obligations.objective: Establish that defined receiving verification is performed and recorded for outsourced special-process product (anodize).
obligations.method: Sample receiving lots for one outsourced process and test whether the defined verification happened.
verificationActivities: Identify the control defined for the anodize provider
Obtain receiving records for lots in the quarter
Sample lots and check each for the defined verification
Where a record is missing, establish whether the verification happened another way
Confirm records are retained where the procedure says
auditQuestions: What verification is defined for this provider’s output and where is that decision recorded?
For the lots received this period, show the verification record for each. Where a record is missing, how do you know the verification happened?
Where verification relies on the provider’s own system or portal, how does the organization retain and retrieve that evidence?
How does verification differ between low-risk and high-risk supplies, and who decided?
What happens to a lot when verification cannot be completed before it is needed in production?
interviewQuestions: (Receiving inspector) Walk me through receiving the last anodize lot. What do you check and where do you record it?
(Purchasing) How do you confirm the provider’s certificate belongs to this lot?
(Quality manager) How would you detect that a lot was released without its verification?

sampling.guidance: Test every receipt if five or fewer. Minimum 4.

riskConsiderations: Evidence held only outside the organization’s retention control
commonFailureIndicators: Certificate held only in a portal not under the organization’s retention control
Verification relied upon but not recorded
alternativeValidImplementations: Provider certificate review plus periodic source or in-process verification
Electronic receiving with certificate attached in the organization’s own system
Reduced verification for a provider with a demonstrated record and a documented rationale

aspects.text: Verification activities are defined for the external provider’s output
The defined verification was performed on received lots

rebuttalChecks.text: Other verification evidence for the lot (packing slip, test report, source inspection)

obligations.shouldBe: The organization determines and applies the verification necessary to ensure externally provided processes, products and services meet requirements, and retains evidence that it was applied.

obligations.title: Effectiveness of actions taken to acquire competence
obligations.interpretation: Where the organization takes action to acquire necessary competence, it evaluates whether the action was effective.
obligations.intent: When the organization acts to close a competence gap, it confirms the action worked, using a method it defines, rather than assuming completion equals competence.
obligations.expectedControl: A defined method and criteria for judging effectiveness, applied after the action, with results recorded and acted on when unsatisfactory.

applicability.note: Applies where competence actions are taken for persons whose work affects conformity of the product or the management system.

obligations.objective: Establish that effectiveness of competence actions is evaluated against defined criteria — by whatever method the organization uses.
obligations.method: Select completed competence actions; for each, find how effectiveness was judged, by whom, against what criteria, and what happened when it failed.
verificationActivities: Determine how required competence is identified
Select completed competence actions
Find the method the organization uses to judge effectiveness
Test that the method was applied to the sampled actions
Examine a case where the result was not satisfactory
auditQuestions: How does the organization decide that a training or other competence action worked? Where is the method and the pass standard defined?
For these completed actions, show the evaluation that followed. Who judged it, against what criteria, and when?
Show a case where the result was unsatisfactory. What happened to the person’s authorization and what did the organization do next?
How is the evaluation result linked to the person and the original action so it can be retrieved?
Where no formal form exists, what other mechanism produces the same assurance and how do you know it is applied every time?
interviewQuestions: (Supervisor) How do you decide someone can work unsupervised after training?
(Employee) What did you have to demonstrate before you were signed off?
(Training coordinator) How do you find out that a training action did not work?
expectedEvidence: Evaluation results (in whatever form the organization uses)

sampling.guidance: Include at least one inspection role and one production role. Minimum 3.

riskConsiderations: Criteria for “effective” left to individual judgement
commonFailureIndicators: Completion recorded but effectiveness never judged
alternativeValidImplementations: A qualification gate in the production system that blocks authorization until observed assessments pass
Supervisor observation against written criteria with a signed record
Post-training performance measures (for example first-pass yield) with defined thresholds

aspects.text: Criteria for judging effectiveness are defined
An evaluation was actually performed after the action
Results are recorded and linked to the action and the person
Action is taken where the evaluation shows the action was not effective

rebuttalChecks.text: Whether the organization controls the same intent through another documented mechanism

obligations.shouldBe: Where actions are taken to acquire the necessary competence, the organization evaluates the effectiveness of those actions.

obligations.title: Validation and control of special processes
obligations.interpretation: Where output cannot be fully verified by later inspection, the process is validated, equipment and personnel are qualified, and the process is kept in control and revalidated when needed.
obligations.intent: Where output cannot be fully verified afterwards, the process itself is proven capable, its equipment and people are qualified, and it is kept in control and revalidated.
obligations.expectedControl: Defined approval criteria; current equipment qualification; qualified personnel; records and defined triggers for revalidation.

applicability.note: Applies only where the organization performs or controls special processes within scope; justify non-applicability if none exist.

obligations.objective: Establish that the in-house heat-treat process is validated and that equipment and personnel qualification are current.
obligations.method: Follow one special process end to end: approval criteria → equipment qualification → personnel → records and revalidation.
verificationActivities: Identify special processes in scope
Review process approval criteria
Verify equipment qualification records and dates
Verify personnel qualification
Check revalidation triggers and records
auditQuestions: Which processes does the organization treat as special and on what basis? Show the list and who maintains it.
For the selected process, show the approval criteria and the record that the process met them.
Show the current equipment qualification (for example a furnace survey): date, result, who performed it, next due date.
Show how personnel qualification is established, recorded and kept current, including expiry.
What changes trigger revalidation (equipment controller change, relocation, parameter change) and show a time it happened.
interviewQuestions: (Process lead) When was the equipment last qualified and where is that record?
(Operator) What stops you running the process if your qualification has lapsed?
(Engineering) What would make you revalidate this process?
riskConsiderations: Latent defects not detectable by inspection
alternativeValidImplementations: Outsourcing to an accredited provider with the organization controlling the approval and verification
Customer-specific special-process approval used as the qualification basis, if recorded

aspects.text: Criteria for review and approval of the process are defined
Equipment qualification is current (e.g. furnace survey)
Records are kept and revalidation is controlled

obligations.shouldBe: Special processes are validated, equipment and personnel are qualified, and records and revalidation are controlled.
